```{r}
library(survival)   # Survival analysis (Cox model, Kaplan-Meier)
library(survminer)  # Visualization of survival curves (ggsurvplot)
library(corrplot)   # Correlation matrix heatmap
library(UpSetR)     # UpSet diagram for set intersections
```

```{r}
load("~/data/fig2.RData")  # Load pre-processed data: all_clinical_miR, miRNA
```


```{r}
# --- 1. Survival analysis: Overall Survival ---

# Fit Cox proportional hazards model for OS to obtain HR and p-value
stats = summary(coxph(Surv(time5, status5) ~ ClassProg2, data = all_clinical_miR))

# Kaplan-Meier estimator stratified by prognostic group (Good vs Poor)
fit <- survfit(Surv(time5, status5) ~ ClassProg2, data = all_clinical_miR)

# Plot KM curves for OS
surv2 = ggsurvplot(
  fit,
  palette = c("#20b2aa", "#DB7093"),                 # Teal = Good, Pink = Poor
  xlab = "Survival time in years",
  ylab = "Probability of overall survival",
  surv.median.line = c("hv"),                        # Horizontal + vertical median lines
  cumcensor = F,
  conf.int = T,                                      # Shaded 95% confidence interval
  risk.table = TRUE,                                 # At-risk table below the plot
  pval = T,                                          # Log-rank p-value on plot
  title = 'Overall Survival (TCGA-OV)',
  risk.table.y.text.col = T,
  risk.table.y.text = FALSE,
  legend.labs = c("Good","Poor"),
  font.main = c(10), font.legend = c(10), font.y = c(10),
  font.x = c(10), font.caption = c(10), font.tickslab = c(10),
  fontsize = 3.4, risk.table.height = 0.3,
  pval.size = 4, censor.size = 6,
  font.ytickslab = c(10)
)

# Fine-tune title and axis label positioning for the OS plot
surv2$plot = surv2$plot + theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.2, size = 9))
surv2$table = surv2$table + theme(
  axis.title.y = element_text(vjust = 2, size = 9),
  axis.title.x = element_text(vjust = -0.2, size = 9),
  plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 9),
  axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9)
) + ggtitle("Number of patients at risk")

surv2
```

```{r}
# --- 2. Survival analysis: Progression-Free Interval ---

# Fit Cox model for PFI to obtain HR and p-value
stats = summary(coxph(Surv(PFI_time5, PFI_status5) ~ ClassProg2, data = all_clinical_miR))

# Kaplan-Meier estimator for PFI stratified by prognostic group
fit <- survfit(Surv(PFI_time5, PFI_status5) ~ ClassProg2, data = all_clinical_miR)

# Plot KM curves for PFI
surv3 = ggsurvplot(
  fit,
  palette = c("#20b2aa", "#DB7093"),
  xlab = "Progression-free interval in years",
  ylab = "Progression-free probability",
  surv.median.line = c("hv"),
  cumcensor = F,
  conf.int = T,
  risk.table = TRUE,
  pval = T,
  title = 'Progression-free interval (TCGA-OV)',
  risk.table.y.text.col = T,
  risk.table.y.text = FALSE,
  legend.labs = c("Good","Poor"),
  font.main = c(10), font.legend = c(10), font.y = c(10),
  font.x = c(10), font.caption = c(10), font.tickslab = c(10),
  fontsize = 3.4, risk.table.height = 0.3,
  pval.size = 4, censor.size = 6,
  font.ytickslab = c(10)
)

# Fine-tune title and axis label positioning for the PFI plot
surv3$plot = surv3$plot + theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.2, size = 9))
surv3$table = surv3$table + theme(
  axis.title.y = element_text(vjust = 2, size = 9),
  axis.title.x = element_text(vjust = -0.2, size = 9),
  plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 9),
  axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9)
) + ggtitle("Number of patients at risk")

surv3
```

```{r}
# --- 3. Arrange both survival plots side-by-side (OS | PFI) ---
splots <- list(surv2, surv3)
p1 = arrange_ggsurvplots(splots, print = TRUE, ncol = 2, nrow = 1, risk.table.height = 0.35)
```

```{r}
# --- 4. UpSet diagram: overlap of miRNA feature selection methods ---
# Each method (DEmiRs, Cox, FCBF, Lasso) produced a set of candidate miRNAs;
# the named vector encodes set sizes and pairwise/higher-order intersections
input = c(
  DEmiRs = 230, Cox = 14, FCBF = 8, Lasso = 78,
  "Cox&DEmiRs" = 2, "FCBF&Lasso" = 2, "DEmiRs&Lasso" = 27,
  "DEmiRs&Lasso&FCBF" = 2, "Cox&DEmiRs&FCBF&Lasso" = 1,
  "Cox&FCBF&Lasso" = 2, "Cox&Lasso" = 2, "Cox&DEmiRs&Lasso" = 9
)

# Plot UpSet diagram to visualise shared and unique miRNAs across methods
p2 = upset(
  fromExpression(input),
  mb.ratio = c(0.6, 0.4),       # 60 % bar chart, 40 % matrix
  number.angles = 0,
  text.scale = 1.5,
  point.size = 2.0,
  line.size = 1,
  main.bar.color = "#B3093F",   # Intersection bar color
  sets.bar.color = "#B3093F",   # Set size bar color
  matrix.color = "#7A8092",     # Dot matrix color
  shade.color = "gray",
  mainbar.y.label = "Number of selected miRNAs"
)
p2
```

```{r}
# --- 5. Correlation matrix of miRNA expression ---

# Spearman correlation on log2-transformed counts (pseudocount +1)
descrCor <- cor(t(log2(miRNA + 1)), method = c("spearman"))

# Subset to miRNAs present in the expression matrix (rows = miRNAs)
descrCor = descrCor[rownames(descrCor) %in% rownames(miRNA), ]
descrCor = descrCor[, colnames(descrCor) %in% rownames(miRNA)]

# Blue-white-red diverging palette (negative to positive correlation)
col <- colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(200)

# Wrap corrplot in ggplotify so it can be combined with patchwork later
p3_plot <- ggplotify::as.ggplot(function() {
  corrplot(
    descrCor,
    col = col,
    order = "hclust",    # Hierarchical clustering to group correlated miRNAs
    type = "full",
    tl.col = "black",
    tl.cex = 0.6,
    number.cex = 0.7,
    cl.cex = 0.7,
    diag = FALSE,        # Hide self-correlations on the diagonal
    mar = c(0, 0, 1, 0)
  )
})

p3_plot
```

```{r fig.height=10, fig.width=10}
# --- 6. Combine survival, UpSet, and correlation plots into Figure 2 ---

# Convert arrange_ggsurvplots output to a ggplot object for patchwork compatibility
p1_plot <- ggplotify::as.ggplot(function() {
  arrange_ggsurvplots(splots, ncol = 2, nrow = 1, risk.table.height = 0.35)
})

p1_plot <- ggplotify::as.ggplot(p1_plot)
p2_plot <- ggplotify::as.ggplot(p2)

library(patchwork)

# Layout: survival plots on top (50 %), UpSet + correlation side-by-side below (80 %)
final_plot <- p1_plot / (p2_plot | p3_plot) + plot_layout(heights = c(0.5, 0.8))
print(final_plot)
```
